headline: Weekend Brief: Global markets brace for heightened energy and geopolitical risk as Iran’s Strait of Hormuz closure looms over Q2 earnings kickoff and key US data
raw_text:
- Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed until further notice, threatening disruption to roughly 20% of global oil flows and intensifying US–Iran tensions
- Elevated oil and fuel prices continue to pressure energy consumers and airlines and weigh on broader consumer sentiment, even as China directs refiners to maintain high fuel output
- US corporate news flow was light over the weekend, with no major M&A deals, pre-announcements, bankruptcies, high-profile earnings pre-releases, or notable analyst calls
- The SEC’s new activist disclosure rules will require investors to reveal client identities in filings, adding transparency that could modestly reshape campaigns, particularly in tech and healthcare
- AWS EMEA’s designation as a ‘Critical Third Party’ by U.K. financial regulators is rippling through the broader technology sector
- Banks are reported to be holding record short positions in bonds, while some strategists warn US equities are “priced for sunshine and rainbows” ahead of an earnings test
- Q2 earnings season formally starts this week, with traders focused on early reads for AI-related spending and consumer resilience
- Major US bank earnings are scheduled to kick off Tuesday, with a heavier earnings ramp expected mid-week
- Key US macro checkpoints later this week include inflation data, retail sales figures, and the June monthly budget statement
- Investors are watching Fed Vice Chair Michelle Bowman’s remarks on financial regulation and Governor Christopher Waller’s comments on the economic outlook, as well as follow-through from Asian and European trading after global markets ended Friday mixed-to-positive
